title: Binary Gauss Stabilizers for Abelian Lattice Gauge Theories
authors: Matteo Turco, Luca Spagnoli, Alessandro Roggero
abstract: Gauge theories and quantum error-correcting codes share the same underlying structure: both use constraints to identify a specific subspace of the full Hilbert space. In quantum error correction, these constraints are known as stabilizers, while in gauge theories they correspond to Gauss law. In this work, we consider a family of discrete Abelian lattice gauge theories described by a $\mathbb{Z}_{N}$ gauge group with $N$ an arbitrary power of two. In this setting, we find a set of stabilizers for the gauge-invariant subspace which is an alternative to the Gauss operators, and we call them binary Gauss stabilizers. We use this alternative stabilizer group to build practical error-correcting codes exploiting the gauge symmetries of the system without the addition of extra qubits. The applications of our finding are not limited to error correction though. We also provide a new strategy of gauge fixing to remove the redundancies based on our alternative stabilizer, which might provide advantages with respect to already-existing approaches such as the axial gauge. Our results provide new tools to study lattice gauge theories and their quantum simulation, and opens directions for future work at the interface of lattice gauge theory and quantum information.
summary: This paper develops 'binary Gauss stabilizers' as an alternative mathematical tool to the standard Gauss operators used to define the physical subspace of Abelian lattice gauge theories. This novel set of stabilizers allows researchers to construct practical quantum error-correcting codes directly from the system's inherent gauge symmetries. The work provides new tools for both understanding lattice gauge theory and advancing quantum simulation techniques.
main_problem: To find an alternative set of stabilizers for Abelian lattice gauge theories that can be used to build practical quantum error-correcting codes without adding extra qubits, and to develop a new strategy for gauge fixing.
main_result: The authors introduce 'binary Gauss stabilizers,' an alternative stabilizer group to the standard Gauss operators, which allows for constructing error-correcting codes exploiting gauge symmetries.
method: The work involves deriving these alternative stabilizers by analyzing the constraints defining the physical Hilbert space and translating them into bitwise equations suitable for quantum circuit representation.
model_or_system: The system is a discrete Abelian lattice gauge theory described by a Z_N gauge group on a hypercubic lattice, coupled with fermionic matter. The Hamiltonian structure involves material, hopping, electric, and plaquette terms.
key_observables: Dimension (D) of the physical Hilbert space; the set of Pauli stabilizers defining the gauge-invariant subspace.
important_parameters: The gauge group order N (specifically Z_{2\eta}); lattice dimension d.
main_assumptions: The analysis initially focuses on 1D and 2D lattices, with generalizations to higher dimensions left for future work. The derivation relies heavily on specific circuit identities for Pauli operator conjugation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate notation (controlled-Z, Toffoli), qubit decompositions for operators on links (e.g., Z_8 theory), and the structure of the derived binary Gauss stabilizers in 1D and 2D.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem by comparing standard Gauss constraints to alternative stabilizer methods. It then derives these 'binary Gauss stabilizers' for 1D and 2D systems, showing their equivalence to the physical subspace defined by Gauss operators. Finally, it details the explicit construction of these generators using quantum circuit identities.
why_interesting: The direct link between gauge symmetries in lattice field theory and stabilizer codes provides a powerful framework for designing fault-tolerant quantum simulations of fundamental physics models.
